hw1:atarashii.tip: An otter rips open a crisp, brand-new sheet. Start on 'ah', not 'oh', and hold the shii long: atarashii.

hw1:shoukai-shimasu.tip: At the kite show, you hold up your kite and introduce it to the crowd. A long, pure shō, and no t: shōkaishimasu.

hw1:jikoshoukai.tip: 自己 jiko means 'self'. Then the show kite from 紹介します: you introduce yourself at the kite show: jikoshōkai.

hw1:onegaishimasu.tip: A horse nudges the stable guy for one more carrot: "Oh, neigh, guy… please!" A short 'neh', not 'nay': onegaishimasu.

hw1:sengetsu.tip: 先 sen is 'before', as in sensei, and 月 getsu is 'month', as in getsuyōbi. The month before: sengetsu.

hw1:kimashita.tip: Your friend came home: their key turns in the front door. A short ki, then mashita with the i almost silent: kimashita.

hw1:madamada-desu.tip: A grand madam praises your Japanese, and you bow: "Madam, madam, I'm still learning." Open 'ah' sounds, and no m at the end: madamada desu.

hw1:onaji.tip: Twins each own a jeep: the same model, the same colour, the same dent. A short, pure o, and a short ji with no p: onaji.

hw1:wakarimashita.tip: A chef tosses curry in a wok, shows you once, and you nod: got it! An open 'kah', not 'kuh': wakarimashita.

hw1:goshusshin.tip: Your hometown's red dirt still cakes your shoe and shin, showing where you're from. Polite go first, a short shu, and hold the sh a beat: goshusshin.

hw1:yuumei.tip: Cameras flash at May the ewe, the most famous sheep in town. Hold the yū long, and say mei almost like 'meh': yūmei.

hw1:goyukkuri.tip: At the hot-spring inn, your host hands you a rice pot: "Go, you cook rice, take your time." A short yu, hold the k, and 'ree', not 'rice': goyukkuri.

1361490.tip: An otter rips open a crisp, brand-new sheet. Start on 'ah', not 'oh', and hold the shii long: atarashii.

1541620.tip: Cameras flash at May the ewe, the most famous sheep in town. Hold the yū long, and say mei almost like 'meh': yūmei.

1387500.tip: 先 sen is 'before', as in sensei, and 月 getsu is 'month', as in getsuyōbi. The month before: sengetsu.

1451750.tip: Twins each own a jeep: the same model, the same colour, the same dent. A short, pure o, and a short ji with no p: onaji.

1612820.tip: An Ohio farmer greets the sunrise over his cornfields: good morning! Say ha, not 'high', and hold the yō long: ohayō.

1002340.tip: This is ohayō plus gozaimasu, the polite add-on you use with teachers and strangers. The final u is almost silent: ohayō gozaimasu.

1289400.tip: こんにち is 今日, 'today', and は is the topic marker, written ha but said wa: 'as for today...'. Say both n's, kon-ni-chi-wa: konnichiwa.

1289480.tip: こんばん is 今晩, 'this evening', and は is written ha but said wa: 'as for this evening...'. The ん before b sounds like m, kom-ban: konbanwa.

1612680.tip: 休み yasumi means 'rest', and the polite お softens it: you're wishing someone a good rest. Three light, even beats, ya-su-mi: oyasumi.

1001780.tip: This is oyasumi plus nasai, a polite tail meaning 'please do', what a child says to their parents at bedtime. Na-sa-i is three beats: oyasumi nasai.

1586820.tip: An alligator holds the door for you, and you say thank you. The r is a quick tap, close to a d, and tō is long with no 'r': arigatō.

1541040.tip: This is arigatō plus the polite gozaimasu, for teachers, shopkeepers and anyone older. The final u is almost silent: arigatō gozaimasu.

1295060.tip: すみ comes from 済む, 'to be settled', and ません means 'not': it isn't settled, I owe you. Five even beats, ending in a hummed n: sumimasen.

2020140.tip: 行って itte is 'go' and 来ます kimasu is 'come': I'll go and come back. The small っ is a short pause before te: itte kimasu.

2088750.tip: Itte is 'go' again, and rasshai is irasshai, 'come', which shopkeepers call out. Pause briefly at both small っ, it-te ras-shai: itte rasshai.

1538960.tip: ただ tada means 'just' and 今 ima means 'now': I'm back just now! Four even beats, ta-da-i-ma, with no stress on da: tadaima.

1612780.tip: 帰り kaeri means 'coming home', and the warm お goes in front. You say it to whoever walks in. Give it three beats, ka-e-ri, with a tapped r: okaeri.

1001740.tip: This is okaeri plus nasai, the same polite tail as in oyasumi nasai: a parent's full welcome home. Say ka-e-ri, not 'carry': okaeri nasai.

1410800.tip: いただき is from いただく, 'to humbly receive', plus ます: hands together, I gratefully receive this food. A short i, then even beats ta-da-ki: itadakimasu.

1270520.tip: ご馳走 gochisō means 'a feast', and さま is the very polite sama: what a feast that was! Hold the sō long and keep ma short: gochisōsama.

1005080.tip: ご馳走 gochisō is 'a feast', and さま is the polite 'Mr.' Bowl empty, you thank Mr. Feast himself. Hold the sō long; the i in shi is nearly silent: gochisōsama deshita.

1625780.tip: 初め hajime means 'the first time'. You wave at someone the first time you meet them. The i in shi is almost silent, 'hajimemash-te': hajimemashite.

2133750.tip: よろしく yoroshiku is 'kindly', and お願いします onegai shimasu is 'please'. Bowing, you ask them to treat you kindly. The final u is almost silent, 'shimas': yoroshiku onegai shimasu.

1413240.tip: 大 dai means 'big', as in daikon, the big radish, and 学 gaku means 'learning'. The big place of learning: daigaku.

1283500.tip: High school kids crowd the school cafeteria for cocoa between classes. Hold both o's long and pure, with no 'w' glide at the end: kōkō.

1206900.tip: 学 gaku is 'study', as in daigaku, and 生 sei is 'life', as in sensei. Someone whose life is study. The ku is often whispered: gakusei.

1413260.tip: 大学 daigaku is 'college', and 生 sei makes it a person, as in gakusei. A college's student, said as one smooth word: daigakusei.

1552750.tip: 留 ryū means 'stay', and gakusei is 'student'. A student who stays in another country to study. Say ryū as one long 'ryoo', not 'ree-oo': ryūgakusei.

1311110.tip: Gliding past on a water ski, I wave at the shore: 'That's me!' Say wah-tah, not 'waw-ter', and end on a soft shi with no k: watashi.

1540170.tip: Tom the tomcat and a dachshund shake paws, best friends. Two short, pure o's in tomo, then dachi with chi as in 'cheese', not 'dax': tomodachi.

1464700.tip: 日本 nihon is 'Japan', and 人 jin is 'person', as in any ～じん nationality. Japan's people, with both n's a full beat: nihonjin.

1288850.tip: An email pings: open it now! Drop the 'ay' and the l, just two short beats, ee-mah: ima.

1269060.tip: Like A.M., 'before midday': 午 go is 'noon' and 前 zen is 'before'. Before noon, a short go and ending on ん: gozen.

1268990.tip: Like P.M., 'after midday': 午 go is 'noon' and 後 go is 'after'. After noon the sun heads down. Two short o's: gogo.

1478750.tip: Look at 半: one stroke runs straight down the middle, cutting it in half. Say 'hahn', ending on ん, not 'hand': han.

genki-1-にじはん.tip: 二 ni is 'two', 時 ji is 'o'clock', and 半 han is 'half': two o'clock and a half. Say 'hahn', not 'han' as in 'hand', and give the ん a full beat: niji han.

1582710.tip: 日 ni is 'sun' and 本 hon is 'origin': where the sun comes from, the land of the rising sun. A short ho, and the ん takes a full beat: nihon.

1464530.tip: 日本 nihon is 'Japan' and 語 go is 'language': Japan's language. Keep the go short and pure, not 'gow': nihongo.

1443840.tip: 電 den is 'electric' and 話 wa is 'talk': electric talk down the wire, the telephone. A short e, and the ん takes its own beat: denwa.

1482290.tip: 番 ban is the 'number ...' you put after a seat or a player, and 号 gō is a number sign too: a phone or room number. Hold the gō long: bangō.

1531710.tip: 名 na is 'name', the kanji read mei in yūmei, and 前 mae is 'front': the name tag pinned to your front. Three even beats, na-ma-e: namae.

2846738.tip: A puzzled diner holds up a naan and asks what it is. Keep the a short, unlike 'naan', and let the ん take a full beat: nan.

1577100.tip: A nanny bends down to a crying baby and asks what's wrong. Say 'nah-nee' with an open a, not the a in 'nanny': nani.

1010080.tip: Asked to come along, your friend answers with a high five: yes! Only the 'high' counts, and it is already a close match: hai.

2837492.tip: そう sō means 'so, that way', and です is 'is': 'It is so', that's right. Hold the ō long, and the u of desu is nearly silent: sō desu.

genki-1-そうですか.tip: Add the question か to sō desu and you get 'Is that so?', the Japanese way to say 'I see.' Let it fall, not rise, when you're just acknowledging: sō desu ka.

1216170.tip: 韓 kan is the Han in Hanguk, Korea's own name for itself, and 国 koku is 'country', as in chūgoku. Say 'kahn', not 'can', with a full-beat ん: kankoku.

1424270.tip: 中 chū is 'middle' and 国 koku, softened to goku, is 'country': China's old name for itself, the Middle Country. Hold the chū long: chūgoku.

genki-1-アジアけんきゅう.tip: アジア is just 'Asia' said the Japanese way, and 研究 kenkyū is 'research', the word for a field of study. A full-beat ん, then a long kyū: ajia kenkyū.

1278010.tip: 工 kō looks like a steel I-beam, and 学 gaku is 'study', as in daigaku and gakusei. The study of building things: engineering. Hold the kō long: kōgaku.

1286430.tip: Two words joined: kokusai, 'international' (国 koku is 'country'), and kankei, 'relations'. Countries shaking hands; give kan's n a full beat: kokusaikankei.

1375970.tip: A wise old sage drops his vote in the ballot box and lectures everyone on politics. Say sei like 'say', and finish with a clear ji, not just 'j': seiji.

1379450.tip: 生物 seibutsu is 'living thing' (生 sei 'life', 物 butsu 'thing'), and 学 gaku is 'study', as in daigaku. The study of living things: seibutsugaku.

1505190.tip: 文 bun is 'writing', as in bunpō, 'grammar', and 学 gaku is 'study', as in daigaku. The study of writing is literature. The u is short, as in 'put': bungaku.

1558050.tip: She dives to an old shipwreck, a piece of history on the seabed. The i of ki is almost whispered, so 'wreck-she' is close; the r is a light tap: rekishi.

1159980.tip: 医 i means 'medicine' and 者 sha means 'person': the medicine person is the doctor. A short i, then sha in one beat: isha.

1198560.tip: 会社 kaisha is 'company' and 員 in means 'member': a company member is an office worker. Kai rhymes with 'sky', and the final n is its own beat: kaishain.

1928100.tip: A nurse bandages a kangaroo's sore paw. Keep the 'kang', then say go, not 'ga', with no 'roo', and end on shi: kangoshi.

1283510.tip: 高 kō is 'high' and 校 kō is 'school', both a long ō, then 生 sei is 'student', as in gakusei. High school student: kōkōsei.

1326160.tip: 主 shu means 'main' and 婦 fu means 'woman': the woman who runs the home. Both vowels short; the fu is soft, lips barely touching, almost 'hoo': shufu.

2077500.tip: Daigaku, 'university', plus 院 in, 'institute', makes graduate school. Add sei, 'student', as in gakusei: daigakuinsei.

1512850.tip: A Bengal tiger in a suit defends his client in court. Keep the 'ben', say go, not 'gal', then shi: bengoshi.

1002650.tip: Mum honks the car horn to pick you up from school. Kā is a long 'kaa' with no r, between the polite o and san: okāsan.

1002590.tip: Dad counts the baby's toes one by one. Hold the tō long, a pure 'oh' with no w glide, between o and san: otōsan.

1001990.tip: Big sister guards the nest while the little ones sleep. Drop the st and hold the e long, 'neh-eh', between o and san: onēsan.

1001830.tip: Big brother drops to one knee to tie your shoe. The nii is just 'knee', held long, between o and san: oniisan.

1524590.tip: Your little sister grabs the TV remote and won't let go. Drop the r, hold the mō long with no w glide, and end on a short to: imōto.

1581930.tip: Little brother wears Dad's tie and copies him. His word sounds like Dad's too: otō as in otōsan, then a short to in place of san: otōto.

1628530.tip: こ ko means near me, and れ re is 'the thing', standing on its own. Hold up the gift in your own hands: kore.

1006970.tip: そ so means near you, and れ re is 'the thing' on its own. Point at the cup in your friend's hands. Say 'soh-reh', not English 'sore': sore.

1000580.tip: あ a means far from us both, and れ re is 'the thing' on its own. Point at the mountain way over there. Say 'ah-reh', not the English 'are': are.

1009290.tip: ど do asks 'which?', and れ re is 'the thing' on its own. Three cakes on the counter, and you ask which one: dore.

1582920.tip: こ ko means near me, and の no always takes a noun after it. Tap the watch on your own wrist, this watch: kono.

1006830.tip: そ so means near you, and の no always takes a noun after it. Point at the bag on your friend's arm, that bag: sono.

1000420.tip: あ a means far from us both, and の no always takes a noun after it. Nod at the student across the hall, that student: ano.

1920240.tip: ど do asks 'which?', and の no always takes a noun after it. Students line up in graduation caps, and you ask which student: dono.

1288810.tip: こ ko means near me, and the second こ ko stands for 'place'. Drop a pin right where you stand: koko.

1006670.tip: そ so means near you, and こ ko stands for 'place'. Point at the chair beside your friend, that spot there: soko.

1000320.tip: あそ aso means far from us both, and こ ko stands for 'place'. You need a telescope to see it, way over there. Not 'ako': asoko.

1577140.tip: ど do asks 'which?', and こ ko stands for 'place'. You stare at the map and ask which place, where: doko.

1416830.tip: Someone knocks on the door: who is it? Darren, again. Drop the n, tap the r lightly, and end on 'eh': dare.

1486650.tip: She slurps an oyster and sighs: delicious! Skip the 'ter'. Say o and i as two quick vowels, then hold the shii long: oishii.

1578010.tip: Put a sock on a fish and it wriggles straight back out. Open 'ah' in every syllable, so the middle is 'kah', not 'kon': sakana.

1457410.tip: A ton of cats crowd round one crispy pork cutlet. A pure 'o' and a full ん in ton, then 'kah', not the 'a' of cats, and a whispered u: tonkatsu.

1463520.tip: A dove on your knee coos over the meat on your plate. Keep 'nee' and 'coo' short, with the u barely there: niku.

1537370.tip: A kid pushes the plate of vegetables away with a 'yah' and a big sigh. A short 'yah', then 'sigh' exactly: yasai.

1301940.tip: It's pouring, and the driver holds an umbrella over you at the car door: "Car, sir?" No r sounds, just 'kah-sah': kasa.

1208910.tip: You pack your bag for a weekend at the cabin. Say 'kah', not 'cab', and end on 'bahn' with a full ん, not 'bin': kaban.

1246700.tip: Two coots, little black water birds, waddle ashore and step into shoes. Say a short ku, and end on a soft, whispered tsu: kutsu.

1296970.tip: A sci-fi alien climbs out of its saucer clutching a fat wallet of space cash. Sai is 'sigh', but fu is a soft, breathy fu, not 'fi': saifu.

1318290.tip: 自 ji is 'self', 転 ten is 'turn', and 車 sha is 'vehicle', as in densha: a vehicle you turn yourself. Keep each vowel short: jitensha.

1362360.tip: 新 shin is 'new', as in Shinkansen, and 聞 bun is 'hear': new things heard, printed every day. The n before b comes out like m: shinbun.

1316140.tip: Kay straps her watch round her big toe to time her swim. Keep to short and pure, with no 'toe-w' glide, then kei like 'Kay': tokei.

1519170.tip: She ties a big bow round the brim of her new hat. Hold the bō long and pure, with no 'w' glide, then a short shi: bōshi.

1522150.tip: 本 is the hon in Nihon, Japan. Picture a thick book called Nihon lying open on your desk. A short, round o, not 'hun' or 'hone': hon.

1243490.tip: 銀 gin is 'silver', as in Tokyo's Ginza, and 行 kō is 'firm': the silver firm that keeps your coins. A hard g, not 'gin' the drink, and hold kō long: ginkō.

1370420.tip: 図 to is 'drawing', 書 sho is 'writing', and 館 kan is 'hall': a hall full of drawings and writings. Keep to and sho short, and kan is 'kahn', not 'can': toshokan.

1542430.tip: You drop your letters into the red bin outside the post office. Hold the yū long, then add kyoku, with kyo as one beat: yūbinkyoku.

1174420.tip: 英 ei is 'England' and 語 go is 'language', as in nihongo: England's language. Say ei like 'ay' in 'day': eigo.

1219980.tip: At the sushi bar you point at the orange salmon roe, ikura, and ask its price: how much? Same sounds; tap the r lightly, near an l: ikura.

1283190.tip: A plain taco with a fifty-dollar price tag makes your eye water: expensive! Say ka like 'kah', not 'co', and run it straight into the eye: takai.

genki-2-をください.tip: 'Could a side of fries come with that?' you ask the cashier: please give me. Drop the d of 'side' and keep the ku light: -o kudasai.

1005900.tip: 'Well then, I'll take the jar,' you say, finally picking one off the shelf. Like 'jar' with no r, the a held long: jā.

1189130.tip: A dozer driver halts and waves you across the site: please, go ahead. Hold the dō long and end on a clear o, not '-er': dōzo.

1009000.tip: A robot bows and sings 'Domo arigato, Mr. Roboto', from the Styx song: thank you. Hold the dō long: dōmo.

1173720.tip: 映 ei is 'project' and 画 ga is 'picture', as in manga. Pictures projected on a big screen. Say ei like 'ay' and ga with an open 'ah': eiga.

1183720.tip: A cook bangs out music on a gong. Drop the g at the front, give ga an open 'ah', and end on a short ku, not 'cook': ongaku.

1002430.tip: 茶 cha is 'tea', the same word that gave English 'chai' and 'a cup of char'. With the polite o in front: ocha.

1371260.tip: At the zoo, an elephant sprays water all over me. A short mi, then a short zu with unrounded lips, not a long 'zoo': mizu.

1586330.tip: 朝 asa is 'morning' and ご飯 gohan is 'rice, a meal'. The morning meal: asagohan.

1602340.tip: 昼 hiru is 'noon' and ご飯 gohan is 'a meal'. The midday meal in your bento box: hirugohan.

1601340.tip: 晩 ban is 'evening', as in konban wa, and ご飯 gohan is 'a meal'. The evening meal: bangohan.

1206730.tip: 学 gaku is 'study', as in gakusei and daigaku, and 校 kō is 'school', as in kōkō. Squeeze gaku to gak, hold the k a beat, and the ō long: gakkō.

1579110.tip: 今 'now' plus 日 'day' make today, with a special reading: the kyō at the end of Tōkyō. One syllable, not 'key-oh', held long: kyō.

1428280.tip: The first morning sun glints on a saw as the carpenter starts work. Both vowels are an open 'ah', not 'uh' or 'aw': asa.

1289470.tip: It's the start of konban wa, 'good evening': 今 kon is 'this' and 晩 ban is 'evening'. This evening, tonight: konban.

1524720.tip: 毎 mai is 'every' and 日 nichi is 'day', as in nichiyōbi. Every day: mainichi.

1524730.tip: 毎 mai is 'every', as in mainichi, and 晩 ban is 'evening', as in konban wa. Every evening, every night: maiban.

1333520.tip: 週 shū is 'week' and 末 matsu is 'end': week-end, word for word, just like English. Hold the shū long and keep the final tsu light: shūmatsu.

1445590.tip: 土 do is 'earth', and 土星 dosei is Saturn: Saturday is Saturn's day in both languages. Hold the yō long: doyōbi.

1464900.tip: 日 nichi is 'sun', so Sunday is the sun's day in both languages. Then 曜日 yōbi, 'day of the week', with a long yō: nichiyōbi.

1221270.tip: A roo drives the car back home after work. Add the eh 'car roo' skips, three beats kah-eh-roo, with a light tapped r: kaeru.

1591110.tip: 聞 is an ear 耳 inside a gate 門: someone listening at the door. Two short beats, kee-koo, the u faint: kiku.

1169870.tip: 飲 is 食 'eat' plus 欠, a person with a wide-open mouth, gulping a drink down. Two short beats, a pure o: nomu.

1562350.tip: 話 is 言 'words' plus 舌 'tongue': words rolling off the tongue as you speak. Three short beats, ha-na-s, the last u almost silent: hanasu.

1358280.tip: The family sits down at the table to eat. Say a short ta, not 'tay', then beh-roo with a tapped r and no l: taberu.

1259290.tip: You see yourself in the mirror. Two short beats, mee-roo, with a pure ee and a light tapped r: miru.

1547720.tip: The ship's crew comes running down the gangway to you. Two beats, koo-roo, not one 'crew': kuru.

1512670.tip: 勉 ben is 'make an effort' and 強 kyō is 'strong': studying is working hard at it. Hold the kyō long, then add suru: benkyō suru.

1404975.tip: おはよう ohayō, 'good morning', grew out of this word: you're up early! Drop the o, keep haya, and end on a short i: hayai.

1584930.tip: Your friends ate the calamari, so there's not much left, just a ring or two. Drop the cal, keep each beat short, tap the r: amari.

1395620.tip: Rain pours on two calm Zen monks, and it bothers them not at all. Say zen twice, each n full: zenzen.

1414580.tip: At the cafe she usually orders a Thai tea. End on a long 'tay', not 'tee': taitei.

1163940.tip: The barista pours you just a little shot of espresso. Start with ch, not sh, pause a beat before to, and end on o: chotto.

1598680.tip: 時 toki is 'time', and 々 repeats it, with the t softening to d: time and time again, sometimes: tokidoki.

1605870.tip: He often dips his toast in an egg yolk. A short, pure yo, not 'yohk', then a faint ku: yoku.

1008460.tip: The demo went perfectly, but then the computer crashed. Say deh-moh, both vowels short and pure: demo.

genki-3-どうですか.tip: どう dō is 'how', and desu ka makes it a polite question. Hold out a cup of tea and ask: how about some? Hold the dō long: dō desu ka.

1589730.tip: You know kaimasu, 'to buy': 買い kai is that buy, and 物 mono is 'thing'. Buying things is shopping: kaimono.

1258330.tip: A dog chases a gnu across the grass. Put a clear, short 'ee' before the gnu, ee-noo: inu.

1467640.tip: A cat jingles the bell round its neck. Keep the e as in 'neck', then add a short, pure o: neko.

1580640.tip: 人 is a person striding on two legs. You know it as jin in Amerikajin; on its own it's read hito, short and crisp: hito.

1307850.tip: 子 ko means 'child', the ko at the end of girls' names like Hanako. Add domo, like dōmo but with both o's short: kodomo.

1223615.tip: A gnat lands right on your nose: yes, you. Every a is a pure 'ah', and add a final ah, ah-nah-tah: anata.

1157070.tip: Flop down into an easy chair. Use an s, not a z, and let the final u almost vanish, ee-su: isu.

1220210.tip: 机 has 木 'tree' on its left: a desk made of wood. Start with tsu as in tsunami, then ku-e, three short beats: tsukue.

1321900.tip: 写 sha is 'copy' and 真 shin is 'true': a true copy of the world is a photo. Both start with 'sh', and it ends on ん: shashin.

1194500.tip: Hannah sniffs a flower from her garden. Open both a's to 'ah', not the a of 'hat', with no stressed beat, hah-nah: hana.

1270590.tip: You've met it in asagohan, hirugohan and bangohan. ご is the polite go; on its own it means cooked rice, or a whole meal: gohan.

2271230.tip: Terracotta tiles cover the temple roof. Put the polite o first, and make the r a light tap, oh-teh-rah: otera.

1273270.tip: Kids drip ice-cream cones all over the park. Hold the kō long, then say en as its own beat, koh-oh-en: kōen.

1098580.tip: バス is 'bus', and 停 tei means 'stop', which is what a bus does there. Say ba-su, then tei like 'tay': basutei.

1490220.tip: A boy in a hospital bed waves from the window. Not 'boy': say b-yo as one beat, hold the ō long, then in: byōin.

1522240.tip: 本 hon is 'book' and 屋 ya is 'shop'. Give the ん its own beat before ya, hon-ya, not ho-nya: hon'ya.

1603990.tip: 町 is 田 'rice field' beside a street: where the fields meet the road, a town grows. Say mah-chee, two short beats: machi.

genki-4-じかん.tip: 時 ji is 'o'clock', as in ichiji, and 間 kan is 'between'. The span between o'clocks is hours. Without kan, two hours becomes two o'clock: -jikan.

1387870.tip: 先 sen is 'before', as in sensei, and 週 shū is 'week', as in shūmatsu. The week before, with the shū held long: senshū.

1315840.tip: 時 is the ji of ichiji, 'one o'clock'. On its own it reads toki, the time when something happens: kodomo no toki, 'when I was a child': toki.

1255890.tip: 月 getsu is 'moon', so Monday is moon day, just as in English. 曜日 yōbi means 'day of the week'. Hold the yō long: getsuyōbi.

1194290.tip: 火 ka is 'fire', so Tuesday is fire day, named for red Mars. A short ka, then hold the yō long: kayōbi.

1372190.tip: 水 sui is 'water', so Wednesday is water day. Say sui quickly, close to 'swee', then hold the yō long: suiyōbi.

1534890.tip: 木 moku is 'tree' or 'wood', so Thursday is tree day. A short, pure o in mo, then hold the yō long: mokuyōbi.

1243320.tip: 金 kin is 'gold' or 'money', so Friday is gold day, like payday. Keep kin and yō apart, kin-yō, not ki-nyō: kin'yōbi.

1198180.tip: Two owls meet on a branch and hoot hello. Drop the l and say both vowels, a then u, in one quick breath: au.

1296400.tip: There is a palm tree on Aruba, there is a beach: aru says a thing is there. Drop the ba, say a as 'ah', tap the r, and end on a short u: aru.

1473740.tip: At the farm shop you buy a cowbell and ring it all the way to the till. Keep only the 'cow', said as two quick beats, ka then u: kau.

1343950.tip: A cuckoo grips a pen in its beak and writes a letter. The first part is 'kah', not 'koo', and the ku is short: kaku.

1298790.tip: Tourists on a tour bus take pictures out of every window. Say a short, pure 'toe', not 'too-er', then a tapped r and a short u: toru.

1410590.tip: At the dojo you kneel on the mats and wait for your turn. Say 'mah', not the a of 'cat', and end with a faint u: matsu.

1606560.tip: わかる is written 分かる, with the 分 of gofun, meaning 'to divide'. Once you can split a problem into parts, you understand it: wakaru.

1577980.tip: A big-eared kangaroo is in the house: iru is for people and animals. Say a short 'ee', not 'ear', and a short ru, not 'roo': iru.

1006980.tip: それ sore is 'that' and から kara is 'from'. From that point on, the next thing happens: and then. Light r's, short vowels: sorekara.

1007310.tip: だ is casual です, 'it is', and から is 'because'. It's raining, dakara, so you grab the umbrella. Every a is a short 'ah': dakara.

1415870.tip: So many tacos bake under the sun that you can't count them. The ku is barely voiced, 'tahk', not 'taco', and san is 'sahn': takusan.

1466940.tip: Why is the shed full of dough? You stare at it, baffled. Hold a pure, long dō, squeeze shi to 'sh', and end on 'teh', not 'd': dōshite.

1163700.tip: 一 is 'one' and 人 is 'person': hitori, one person on their own. で means 'by', so by oneself, alone: hitori de.

1171010.tip: A MiG jet banks hard to the right. Both i's are 'ee', not the short i of 'MiG', and add a final gi: migi.

1392580.tip: You know 名前 namae, 'name': its 前 is mae. Your name badge goes on the front of your shirt. Two vowels, 'mah-eh': mae.

1269410.tip: The usher leads you all the way to the back row. Start with 'oo', not 'uh', say 'shee', not 'sher', and a light r: ushiro.

1423310.tip: Bang the door knocker and you're let inside, out of the rain. Both vowels are 'ah' and there's no r: naka.

1352130.tip: 上 is a mark standing on top of a line, like a strawberry sitting on a cake. Two vowels, 'oo' then 'eh': ue.

1184140.tip: 下 hangs down below its line, like a fish swimming under the water's surface. The i is barely voiced, almost 'shtah': shita.

1242160.tip: A chick hops near a cook, close enough to peck her apron. Say 'chee', not 'chick', 'kah', not 'uh', and end on 'koo', no final k: chikaku.

1555830.tip: Ghibli's My Neighbor Totoro is Tonari no Totoro: the neighbour lives right next door. Short o, a light r: tonari.

1215230.tip: 間 is the sun 日, as in nichiyōbi, shining between the two doors of a gate 門. Three vowels, 'ah-ee-dah': aida.

1358340.tip: 食べ tabe is from taberu, 'to eat', and 物 mono is 'thing'. Things you eat: tabemono.

1600430.tip: 飲み nomi is from nomu, 'to drink', and 物 mono is 'thing', as in tabemono. Things you drink: nomimono.

1193060.tip: A barracuda snaps a bunch of fruit off a branch hanging over the water. Keep only the cuda, a short 'koo-dah', then 物 mono 'thing', as in tabemono: kudamono.

1227500.tip: 休 is a person 亻 leaning against a tree 木, taking a rest: a day off. Three short beats, ya-su-mi: yasumi.

1553170.tip: Leo the lion boards a coach to travel the country. Ryo is one quick syllable with a light r, not 'lee-oh'. Hold the kō long and drop the ch: ryokō.

1002500.tip: お is the polite o, 土 is 'earth' and 産 is 'produce': something made in the local land, carried home for friends. Say mi-ya-ge, ge like 'geh': omiyage.

1438690.tip: 天 ten is 'sky' and 気 ki is 'spirit, mood', as in genki. The sky's mood: tenki.

1337270.tip: 宿 shuku is 'lodging', the place you stay, and 題 dai is 'topic'. A topic you take home with you: shukudai.

1419110.tip: Sun-tanned Joe blows out the candles on his birthday cake, and 日 bi is 'day', as in getsuyōbi. Say tan as 'tahn', and hold the jō long: tanjōbi.

1499320.tip: Someone has stuffed your room with hay, floor to ceiling. Say he as a short 'heh', not 'hay', then ya: heya.

1521400.tip: A boy holds up the bok choy he grew and points to himself: 'I grew this!' Keep only the bok, with a pure o, not 'bahk', and a light u: boku.

1265070.tip: An old furry teddy bear sits in the attic, its fur worn thin with age. Say fu-ru-i, three short beats, with u not 'er': furui.

1343460.tip: 暑 has the sun 日 on top: hot weather, the air itself. Three short beats, with tsu as in tsunami: atsui.

1210360.tip: 寒 has two little ice dots at the bottom, under a roof: cold weather. Three short beats, sa-mu-i: samui.

1467720.tip: 熱 has four fire dots 灬 along the bottom: hot to the touch, like a kettle or a bath. Same sound as 暑い for hot weather: atsui.

1519290.tip: 忙 is a heart 忄 beside 亡 'lost': so busy you've lost your heart. Say i-so-ga, then hold the shii long: isogashii.

1588880.tip: 大 is a person stretching their arms out wide: big, as in daigaku. Hold both long vowels, the ō and the kii: ōkii.

1347750.tip: A mouse sighs over a cheese so small it fits on a fingertip. Hold the chii long, with no z, and sai rhymes with 'sigh': chiisai.

1533580.tip: 面 is 'face' and 白 is 'white': a face lit up bright with interest. Five short beats, o-mo-shi-ro-i: omoshiroi.

1157000.tip: Making sashimi is easy: just slice the fish, no cooking. Put ya in front, drop the mi, and hold the shii: yasashii.

1460850.tip: A moose tries counting a mountain of cash and gives up: too difficult. Short mu-zu with a z, 'kah' not 'cash', and a long shii: muzukashii.

1577490.tip: A koi in sunglasses drives a sports car, looking so good. Say car as 'kah' with no r, pause on the っ, then ko and a long ii: kakkoii.

1593480.tip: A ghost leaps out at a cow, who moos 'Why?!' It's frightening. Say ko with a pure o, not 'cow', then wa-i as two quick beats: kowai.

1207240.tip: You lie on a sheet getting a tan at the beach: such fun! Say ta as 'tah', skip the 'a', drop the t, and hold shii long: tanoshii.

1153670.tip: The sign says chop suey for one coin: so inexpensive! Swap 'chop' for a short ya, then say su-i as two quick beats, not 'sooey': yasui.

1277450.tip: Sue is so fond of her skis that she hugs them. The u is nearly silent, so say 'ski' with no s at the end: suki.

1413660.tip: 大 dai is 'big', as in daigaku, and 好き suki is 'fond of'. A big fondness means you love it: daisuki.

1413610.tip: 大 dai is 'big', as in daigaku, and 嫌い kirai is 'dislike'. A big dislike means you hate it: daikirai.

1260720.tip: Your textbook GENKI is named for it: full of health and energy. 気 ki is 'spirit', as in 天気 tenki. A hard g, and e as in 'get': genki.

1381820.tip: 'Shh!' The zoo car creeps quietly past the sleeping lion. Shi is like 'she', and zu and ka are short, with no r: shizuka.

1463480.tip: A yacht serves nigiri to a lively, noisy party on deck. Drop the ri from nigiri, and say yacht as a short 'yah-kah', not 'yot': nigiyaka.

1577280.tip: Not busy at last, you have time to trek the Himalayas. Keep only hi-ma: hi as 'hee', not 'him', and a short 'mah': hima.

1174340.tip: You dive in to swim and the pool is full of yogurt: 'Oh, yogurt!' Keep three short beats, o-yo-gu, with no 'rt' at the end: oyogu.

1591110-きく-5.tip: 聞 is an ear 耳 inside a gate 門: you lean in at the gate to ask, then listen for the answer. Two short beats, ki-ku: kiku.

1355120.tip: You try to ride a kangaroo and it bounces you off: 'No, roo!' Say no with a pure o, then a light, flapped r and a short u: noru.

1598550.tip: 出 de is 'out', as in 出口 deguchi, the exit sign. You step out through the exit door. Four even beats with a light r, de-ka-ke-ru: dekakeru.

1163420.tip: 一 is 'one', as in ichi: everyone moving as one, together. Hold the っ as a short pause before sho: issho ni.

2272830.tip: It's すごい sugoi, 'amazing', with the final い swapped for く so it can boost another word: amazingly, extremely. A short u in su: sugoku.

1414150.tip: Jo drips dye on her boot, shrugs and says it's okay. Hold the jō long and drop the t: dai-jō-bu: daijōbu.

1009330.tip: It's the ど question word, like どれ and どこ, in the こんな/そんな/あんな set: what kind of ice cream? Hold the ん a full beat: donna.

1237020.tip: 教 kyō is 'teach', 科 ka is 'subject' and 書 sho is 'writing'. Writing that teaches a subject is a textbook. Hold the kyō long: kyōkasho.

1001820.tip: Grandma stuffs her money into an old tin can. Say kah-neh, two short beats, not 'can', with the polite o in front: okane.

1195430.tip: 荷 ni is a 'load' and 物 is 'thing', the mono of tabemono. Loaded-up things are your baggage; here 物 reads motsu, with a light tsu: nimotsu.

1443000.tip: 電 den is 'electric', as in denwa, the phone, and 気 ki is 'energy', as in genki. Electric energy is electricity: denki.

1401400.tip: A mad dog presses its nose against the window, barking. Say mah, not 'mad', drop the g, and keep a pure short o: mado.

1443530.tip: 電 den is 'electric', as in denki, and 車 sha is 'vehicle', as in jitensha, the bicycle. An electric vehicle on rails is a train: densha.

1592250.tip: 国 is a border box with 玉, a jewel, inside: a treasure guarded inside borders is a country. Short koo, short nee: kuni.

1289220.tip: 今 kon is 'now', as in konban wa, and 週 shū is 'week', as in senshū. The week we're in now is this week. Hold the shū long: konshū.

1548010.tip: 来 rai is 'coming', the same kanji as kimasu, and 週 shū is 'week'. The coming week is next week. Hold the shū long: raishū.

1548220.tip: 来 rai is 'coming', as in kimasu, and 年 nen is 'year', as in ichinensei. The coming year is next year: rainen.

1536350.tip: Night falls and the moon settles on your roof. Say yo-roo, two short beats, with a light tapped r and no f: yoru.

1415000.tip: A hen in a necktie is having a tough day at the office, feathers everywhere. Tai like 'tie', then a clear hen: taihen.

1350110.tip: It's the kesu of keshigomu, the eraser: it wipes things out, like a candle you put out or a light you turn off. Say 'kess', the u almost silent: kesu.

1310730.tip: 死 shi means 'death', which is why 4 is usually read yon rather than shi. Add nu to make it a verb, to die. Two short beats: shinu.

1597040.tip: A sailor stands up to show off his anchor tattoo. Keep both a's short, and make the second sound tsu, t-s as in 'cats', the u almost silent: tatsu.

genki-6-たばこをすう.tip: Tabako is just 'tobacco', and 吸う suu means 'to breathe in', a long soo like drawing in smoke. To breathe in tobacco is to smoke: tabako o suu.

1305990.tip: Two cats use a sleepy cow as a ladder up to the hayloft. Say tsu like the 'ts' in 'cats' with a faint u, and kau rhymes with 'cow': tsukau.

1328190.tip: The tent's down in the wind, so the whole campsite rushes to help put it back up. Drop the n of 'tent', and dau has no n either: tetsudau.

1465590.tip: A roo leaps high to enter the house through an open window. Say hai like 'high', then a short, light ru, not a long 'roo': hairu.

1315720.tip: A soldier carries heavy buckets of water to fill the castle moats. Keep mo short, not 'moh-oh', and tsu is the 'ts' of 'moats' with a faint u: motsu.

1227560.tip: 休 is the same kanji as 休み yasumi, a day off. Yasumu is the verb: you take the day off and are absent from class: yasumu.

1589500.tip: An oriole hops down and gets off the bus at its stop. Start with a short, pure o, not 'or', and end on a light ru instead of 'ole': oriru.

1323560.tip: A caribou borrows a library book, promising to bring it back next week. Keep ka as 'kah', not 'care', and swap the bou for a short ru: kariru.

2836288.tip: シャワー is just 'shower'. Picture a bee taking a shower under a dripping tap. Say a as 'ah', not 'uh', keep bi short, and add a light ru: shawā o abiru.

1443840-でんわする-6.tip: 電話 denwa is the 'telephone' you already know, and する turns it into a verb: to call someone. Keep the n before wa: denwa suru.

1610460.tip: くる is 'come', and つれて is from tsureru, 'take someone along'. You come with a person in tow; for things, say motte kuru instead: tsurete kuru.

1315710.tip: もって comes from motsu, 'carry', and くる is 'come': carry it and come, so you bring a thing. Pause on the small っ: motte kuru.

1269350.tip: A toad yawns on its lily pad and promises to catch flies later on. Say a as 'ah', keep to short, not 'toe', and finish the d with a short e: ato de.

1430610.tip: Drop sugar into hot tea and it melts right away. Start with a plain s, not the 'sh' of sugar, barely say the u, and end on a short gu, not 'gar': sugu.

genki-6-けっこうです.tip: A waiter offers a gecko a fly, and the gecko gives a thumbs up: that would be fine. Start with k, not g, pause on the っ, and stretch the ō: kekkō desu.

genki-6-ほんとうですか.tip: 本 hon is 'book', but also 'real', and 当 tō is 'on the mark'. Is that real and on the mark? Really? Stretch the tō: hontō desu ka.

1192150.tip: The whole family marches round the house, each blowing a kazoo. Say ka as 'kah', not 'kuh', keep zo short, not 'zoo', then add a light ku: kazoku.

1002320.tip: Grandpa wears a cap with a big gold G on it. Hold the jii long like the letter G; a short ji gives ojisan, 'uncle': ojiisan.

1002330.tip: Grandma always pulls a chocolate bar from her handbag for you. Say bā as a long open 'ah' with no r; a short ba gives obasan, 'aunt': obāsan.

1497610.tip: Dad plants a kiss on each cheek, cheek, then the other. Drop the k sounds and keep both 'chee' beats short. Used for your own father: chichi.

1514990.tip: Mum laughs 'ha ha' at every joke you tell her. Two short, breathy 'hah' beats, not drawn out. Used for your own mother: haha.

1249900.tip: Your big brother crashes his skateboard and scrapes a knee. Start on an open 'ah', not 'uh', and keep the nee short: ani.

1307630.tip: Your big sister plays goalie and guards a net. Open 'ah', drop the t, end on a short 'eh'; ani with 'ee' is brother: ane.

1249960.tip: 兄 is ani, 'older brother', and 弟 is 'younger brother': put them together for all the siblings. Kyō is long, as in Kyōto; dai as in daigaku: kyōdai.

1420020.tip: 男 is 田 'rice field' over 力 'power': the one putting his strength into the field. Three short o's, then の人 'person': otoko no hito.

1344980.tip: The woman behind the counter is the owner of the shop, keys in hand. Short o, hold the n an extra beat (on-na), end on 'nah', then の人: onna no hito.

1198550.tip: You met 会社員 kaishain, 'office worker', in lesson 1. Drop the 員 'member' and you're left with the company itself: kaisha.

1358550.tip: 食 is the 'eat' of 食べる, and 堂 means 'hall': an eating hall. Say sho-ku with a short ku, then a long dō: shokudō.

1275640.tip: A cookie goes into a wide-open mouth, square like the kanji 口. Swap the 'kie' for a short 'chee', and keep ku short: kuchi.

1604890.tip: 目 is an eye drawn upright: the frame of the lids with the eye inside. Say it 'meh', never 'me': me.

1577670.tip: Glasses are 'eye metal': 目 me 'eye' plus kane 'metal', as in okane, money. The k softens to g, and ne is 'neh', not 'nee': megane.

1193180.tip: A girl hums a happy song as her scooter rolls downhill. Drop the 'sc', and end on a clean, short ta, not 'ter': uta.

1323080.tip: 車 is a cart seen from above: a box on an axle with a wheel at each end. Three short beats, the r a light tap: kuruma.

1429750.tip: The old nag grows a mane so long it sweeps the ground. Use an open 'ah' in na, not the a of 'nag', then ga-i: nagai.

1404975-はやい-7.tip: With a sharp 'Hiyah!' the karate master's chop is too fast to see. Open with 'hah', not 'hi', and add a short ee at the end: hayai.

1472660.tip: 高い takai is 'high' from lesson 2, and 背が puts 'height' in front: your height is high. Se is a short 'seh': se ga takai.

1472670.tip: The same 背が 'height' as se ga takai, with 低い hikui, 'low', the opposite of takai: your height is low. Hee-koo-ee, all short: se ga hikui.

2146840.tip: A bright kid balances a tomato on her head, 頭 atama, and gets a good idea. Every vowel is 'ah', a-ta-ma, with no 'toe' at the end: atama ga ii.

1365250.tip: 親 is 'parent' and 切 is 'cut': a kind parent cuts your food into small bites. Shin as in your shin, then setsu with a quick, soft u: shinsetsu.

1512610.tip: A bendy straw is so convenient: you sip without lifting the cup. Say ben, then ri with a light tapped r, close to the d in 'bendy': benri.

1588120.tip: 歌 uta is 'song', and the verb ending う turns it into an action: song + u, to sing. Two short, plain u sounds, never 'yoo': utau.

1484330.tip: Before every shift, the cab driver puts on the cap he keeps on the cab roof. Say kah, a short bu, a light tapped ru and no f: kaburu.

1607260.tip: You hack the legs off old jeans with scissors, then put on your new shorts. Open the a to 'hah', and add a short ku that 'hack' doesn't have: haku.

1420470.tip: A shrew gets to know its new burrow, sniffing out every corner. Slip a short i in after the sh, then a light tapped ru: shiru.

genki-7-しっています.tip: From 知る shiru, 'get to know'. Once you've got to know something, you're in that state: 'I know'. Hold the っ as a short pause before te: shitte imasu.

genki-7-しりません.tip: 知り from shiru, 'get to know', plus the polite negative ません: 'I don't know'. No っ here, and end on a clean n: shirimasen.

1334040.tip: Sue lives in a little cottage with her cow, and it moos at her from the garden every morning. Two short u's, no long 'oo': sumu.

1451150.tip: Office workers hang their hats on the hat rack, then get to work. Add an a between hat and rack, tap the r lightly, and end on ku: hataraku.

1408220.tip: Lounging on a futon eating cake all winter, you gain weight. Drop futon's n and add a light tapped ru: futoru.

genki-7-ふとっています.tip: From 太る futoru, 'gain weight'. Having gained it, you're in that state: on the heavy side. Hold the っ as a short pause before te: futotte imasu.

1911810.tip: めがね megane is 'glasses', and かける kakeru is 'hang': you hang your glasses on your ears. Glasses take their own verb: megane o kakeru.

1423000.tip: 着 is the ki in kimono 着物, a 'wear-thing'. You put on a kimono, shirt or coat with this verb, a short ki and a light ru: kiru.

genki-7-やせています.tip: From やせる yaseru, 'lose weight'. Having lost it, you're in that state: thin. Unlike futotte, there's no っ here: yasete imasu.

1254790.tip: The bride and groom share one cake cone at the altar. Say keh, not 'cake', pause on the っ, and a short kon, not 'cone': kekkon suru.

1188490.tip: 何 nani is 'what', and も is 'even': with a negative, not even a 'what', so nothing at all: nanimo.

1576150.tip: Like hitotsu, 'one thing', it starts with hito, and ri counts people: one person, an irregular form, not ichinin: hitori.

1582670.tip: Like futatsu, 'two things', it starts with futa, and ri counts people: two people, an irregular form, not ninin: futari.

1535780.tip: Offered a plate of sweet mochi, of course you grab one! A short mo, then ron with a tapped r and a clean n: mochiron.

1554530.tip: よかった yokatta is 'it was good', and ら adds 'if': if it's good for you, so 'if you like'. Hold the っ as a short pause: yokattara.

1376460.tip: A hare stretches out on the grass, basking in the sunny weather. Say hah-reh, two short beats with a light tapped r, not 'hair': hare.

1171900.tip: A mare stands out in the rain, her mane dripping. Say ah-meh: two short beats, an open ah, and no r: ame.

1592340.tip: 曇 puts 日, the sun, over 雲 kumo, 'cloud': the sun lost in cloud. Add ri for three short beats: kumori.

1386500.tip: Snow buries a log cabin in the Yukon. Keep the yu short, then end on a short kee instead of 'kon': yuki.

1438770.tip: 天気 tenki is 'weather' and 予報 yohō is 'forecast': the weather forecast on TV. Hold the final hō long: tenkiyohō.

1221950.tip: 気 ki is the air, as in tenki, and 温 on means 'warm'. How warm the air is: the temperature. Two beats, ki then on: kion.

1191320.tip: Gnats swarm around your head on a hot summer evening. Say nah, not the 'a' in gnat, and end with a soft, whispered tsu: natsu.

1446070.tip: In winter you pump fuel to heat the house. Split it into two short beats, foo-yoo, with a soft breathy f and no l: fuyu.

1579100.tip: 今 is 'this' and 朝 asa is 'morning', but together they take a special short reading, keh-sah, not kon-asa: kesa.

1584640.tip: You'll grill a satay the day after tomorrow, at the weekend party. Say ah-sat-teh, with a catch on the っ and a short teh, not 'tay': asatte.

1524690.tip: 毎 mai is 'every', as in mainichi, and 週 shū is 'week', as in raishū. Every week, with the shū held long: maishū.

1289100.tip: 今 kon is 'now' or 'this', as in konbanwa, and 月 getsu is 'month', as in getsuyōbi. This month: kongetsu.

1547900.tip: 来 rai is 'coming', as in raishū, and 月 getsu is 'month', as in getsuyōbi. The coming month: raigetsu.

1304970.tip: A she-goat trots off to her job with a briefcase in her mouth. Keep shi short, then go-to with two pure, short o's, not 'goat': shigoto.

1343100.tip: A crow lands on your toe: it has found its place. Give it three even beats, to-ko-ro, short pure o's and a light tapped r: tokoro.

1476410.tip: You scoop up crispy potato hash with your chopsticks. Say hah-shee: an open ah, not the 'a' in hash, plus a short ee: hashi.

2220600.tip: A farmer floods a furrow and lies back in it for a warm bath. お is the polite prefix, then fu-ro, two short beats with no 'er': ofuro.

1188270.tip: 何 nani is 'what'. Add か and 'what?' becomes a thing you can't name: something. Nani plus ka: nanika.

1353320.tip: 上 is 'up' and 手 is 'hand': someone with the upper hand is skillful. Hold the jō long and end on a short zu: jōzu.

1185200.tip: 下 is 'down' and 手 is 'hand': a hand that keeps letting you down is clumsy. Two short beats, heh-tah: heta.

1390930.tip: A raccoon washes its food in the stream before eating. Keep 'a ra', swap the coon for a short u, and tap the r: three quick beats: arau.

1587040.tip: 言 is a 口 mouth with lines of words rising above it: to say. Written iu, but said like one long 'yoo', yū: iu.

1546640.tip: To hear the teacher, you need your ear. Then add a quick tapped r and a short u, ee-roo: iru.

genki-8-おそくなる.tip: You'll be late again because you can't find your other sock. Say o-so-ku with pure short vowels, then naru, 'become': osoku naru.

1002600.tip: A hairy roo hops into a steaming bathtub. お風呂 ofuro is 'bath' and に ni 'into'; hairu is hai-ru, short, with a flicked r: ofuro ni hairu.

1589350.tip: A farmer stops a mower mid-field to sit and think. Three short beats, o-mo-u, pure o's with no 'er', and a light u: omou.

1384830.tip: A boat's sharp keel cuts the waves like scissors. Two short beats, ki-ru, ending in a flicked r and a light u, not an English l: kiru.

1597890.tip: Two crews work side by side to make a house. Start with tsu, a t pressed into s, keep every u short, and no z at the end: tsukuru.

1282790.tip: Rain falls on the fruit stall, drumming on every apple. Drop the t, and give fu and ru two short, equal beats: furu.

1315700.tip: 持って motte is 'holding' and いく iku is 'go': go holding it, so take it along. Hold the っ, a short pause before te: motte iku.

1322320.tip: He throws a broken old stereo into the bin. The su is barely voiced, so it's s-teh-ru, ending in ru, not 'ree-oh': suteru.

1307550.tip: You already know はじめまして, said when you first meet, as things begin. Same root, verb form: hajimeru.

1172830.tip: You drive to the campsite with a tent strapped to the roof. Put a short un, like 'oon', before ten, and drop the final t: unten suru.

1390980.tip: A centaur scrubs his laundry in the river with soap. Sen like 'send', a short ta with no r, then a light ku: sentaku suru.

1399790.tip: A soldier sweeps the barracks clean for inspection. No l: hold the sō long, then a short ji like 'jee', not 'jer': sōji suru.

1554310.tip: 料理 ryōri is 'cuisine', and する suru is 'to do'. Doing cuisine means cooking: ryōri suru.

1188890.tip: いつ itsu is 'when', and も mo turns it into 'every when': any time you ask, it's so. The i is short and the su almost silent: itsumo.

1421980.tip: He's out late again, still hunting for a sock. Pure o at the front, not 'uh', and end on a light ku, not 'k': osoku.

1590950.tip: 乾 kan is 'dry' and 杯 pai is 'cup': raise your glass and drain the cup dry. The n comes out like m before p: kanpai.

genki-8-みんなで.tip: A school of minnows swims all together, every fish in step. Say min-na with a doubled n and a final a, not 'nose', then de: minna de.

genki-8-ざんねんですね.tip: 残 zan is 'left over' and 念 nen is 'feeling': the feeling left over when plans fall through. Hold both n's, zan-nen: zannen desu ne.

1008910.tip: A doe stops at the edge of a stream and tilts her head: how do I get across? Hold the ō long and pure, with no 'w' glide at the end: dō.

1417330.tip: Two tango dancers spell out a word with their steps across the floor. Say ta with a pure 'ah', give the n its own beat, and keep go short: tango.

1297960.tip: A student writes her whole essay on a bakery sack, a bun still inside. Sa is 'sah', ku is light, and bun is a short 'boon', not 'bun': sakubun.

1312350.tip: A chicken sits the exam with a pencil in its beak. Start with sh, not ch, and say ken, not 'kin': shiken.

1327720.tip: 手 te is 'hand' and 紙 kami is 'paper', as in origami, with the k softened to g. Paper written by hand is a letter: tegami.

1490230.tip: 病気 ends in the same 気 ki as genki. Genki is well; put 病 byō, 'sick', in front and you're ill. Byo is one sound, not 'bee-oh', with the ō held long: byōki.

1835640.tip: いい ii is 'good' and 子 ko is 'child', as in kodomo. Hold the ii long. A good child: iiko.

1357600.tip: Euro notes come in every colour: green, blue, orange, purple. Drop the 'y' and start on a clear 'ee', then a quick tapped ro with a short, pure o: iro.

1289370.tip: Cranes are building your new condo, and you'll move in soon, in the near future. Kon has a pure o and a full n beat, and do is short: kondo.

1231690.tip: 年 nen is 'year', as in ichinensei, and 去 kyo means 'gone'. The year that's gone: last year. Kyo is one short beat, not 'key-oh': kyonen.

1381390.tip: A sailor shouts 'Ahoy!' from his boat across the deep blue sea. There's no h, just three short, pure vowels, a-o-i: aoi.

1383240.tip: You paddle a bright red kayak down the river. Stop before the last 'yak': three short beats, a-ka-i, with a pure 'ah': akai.

1287420.tip: A crow dips its feathers in ink and comes out black. Put a quick u after the k, ku-ro, with a pure o, then a short i: kuroi.

1579720.tip: A lonely bee sits by itself on a flower and lets out a sob. Sob-bee gives sa-bi, with a pure 'ah'; end with a long shii: sabishii.

1538440.tip: A doe and a kangaroo dance cheek to cheek under the lights. Put a short o in front, keep both o's pure, and make ru a quick tap, not 'roo': odoru.

genki-9-くすりをのむ.tip: 飲む nomu is 'to drink', as in nomimasu. In Japanese you drink medicine, even a pill: kusuri o nomu.

2847376.tip: 人 nin is 'people' and 気 ki is the feeling in genki. When people's warm feeling is there (ga aru), it's popular. The n is its own beat: ninki ga aru.

1307500.tip: It starts with the same hajim- as hajimemashite, which you say when a meeting first begins. The clapper snaps and the film begins: hajimaru.

1419370.tip: A hiccup jolts your hands as you play the piano. Say hee-koo, both short, 'koo' not 'kuh', with no 'p' on the end: hiku.

1535910.tip: A friend hands you one more owl, and you get it for your collection. Three short beats, mo-ra-u, the r a light tap: morau.

1206050.tip: An oboe player memorizes her part, then plays with the music shut. Say oh-boh-eh, all short with no glide, then a light ru: oboeru.

1338240.tip: A dairy cow appears in the barn doorway, poking her head out. Keep the 'deh' of dairy, then a light ru, not 'ree': deru.

1172910.tip: Exercise is the undo button for last night's cake: you work it off. Say oon, not 'un', and a long doh, not 'doo': undō suru.

1303620.tip: Sam takes his pony for a slow walk round the park. Say sahm-po: 'ah', not Sam's 'a', ん sounds like m before p, and no 'ny': sanpo suru.

1374530.tip: 是 means 'right' and 非 'wrong': right or wrong, come anyway, by all means! Ze as in 'zen', then a short hee: zehi.

1343110.tip: ところ is 'place' and で is 'at': at this place in the chat, you turn to a new topic. By the way: tokorode.

1202150.tip: A whole school of minnows swims off together, all of them at once. Hold the n for an extra beat and end on 'nah', not 'no': minna.

1012480.tip: The ride-on mower has already cut the whole lawn before you wake up. Say 'mow', held long, with no 'er': mō.

1341000.tip: Every spring a farmer drags a harrow across the field, ready for planting. Say a flat 'hah', and end on a short ru, not 'oh': haru.

1332650.tip: An Akita dog bounds through a heap of fall leaves. Akita, 秋田, really means 'autumn field'. Drop the -ta, open 'ah', then a short ki: aki.

1231590.tip: 牛 gyū is 'cow', as in gyūdon, and 乳 nyū is 'milk': cow's milk. Both halves are long: gyū rhymes with 'cue', nyū with 'new': gyūnyū.

1555480.tip: At the fair you toss a ring and it drops neatly round a shiny red apple. Add a short go, and tap the r lightly, near a soft d: ringo.

1554310-りょうり-10.tip: Rory the lion travels the world tasting every country's cuisine. Glide the r and y into one beat, hold the ō long, and tap the r lightly: ryōri.

1537300.tip: A yak swings a pool cue like a bat and smacks a baseball. Say 'yah', not the flat a of yak, and kyū as one long 'cue': yakyū.

2429350.tip: お金 okane is 'money', and 持ち mochi, like the rice cake, comes from 持つ motsu, 'to have': someone who has money. All vowels short: okanemochi.

1541630.tip: 有名 yūmei is 'famous', and 人 jin is 'person', as in nihonjin: a famous person. Hold the yū long: yūmeijin.

1217730.tip: A toddler drinks hot cacao and grins with chocolate all over his face. Use only the end of cacao, 'kah-oh', two clear vowels, not 'cow': kao.

1468870.tip: 年 toshi is 'year' or 'age', and 上 ue is 'above', as in つくえの上: above you in years. Say u-e as two short vowels: toshiue.

1420900.tip: 地 chi is 'ground', 下 ka is 'under' (the した in つくえの下), and 鉄 tetsu is 'iron', for the rails: the iron road underground. All short: chikatetsu.

1602800.tip: A big ship puffs smoke from its tall funnel as it leaves port. Say fu like 'food', not 'fun', and end on 'neh' with no l: fune.

1485470.tip: 飛 hi is 'fly', 行 kō is the 'go' of 行く and ginkō, and 機 ki is 'machine': a fly-and-go machine. Hold the kō long: hikōki.

1543750.tip: A yak phones a restaurant: 'Yo! A table for one yak.' Its reservation is made. Say yo once, then two light beats ya-ku, not 'yack': yoyaku.

1451490.tip: 動 'move' plus 物 'thing' makes dōbutsu, 'animal', and 園 en is 'garden'. A garden of animals. Hold the dō long and end on n: dōbutsuen.

1315920.tip: 時 ji is 'o'clock', as in ichiji, and 間 kan is 'between'. The stretch between the hours is time. Say kan with 'ah', not 'can': jikan.

1373860.tip: A sea kayak paddles all the way around the world. Say se as a short 'seh', not 'see', and drop the final 'ak': sekai.

1486680.tip: 美容 biyō is 'beauty care', and 院 in is a place, as in byōin 'hospital'. Keep the extra i, or you're at the hospital: biyōin.

1328090.tip: 手 te is 'hand', and 袋 fukuro is 'bag', softened to bukuro. A bag for your hand: tebukuro.

1378860.tip: 生 sei is 'life', as in gakusei, and 活 katsu is 'lively'. Lively living, your daily life. Say sei like 'say', and katsu's u is barely there: seikatsu.

1579130.tip: 今 is 'this', as in konban and konshū, and 年 toshi is 'year'. This year, but say ko with no n: kotoshi.

1586420.tip: A tot warms up by the fire: 'a tot' plus takai, the word you know for 'expensive'. Every a is a short 'ah': atatakai.

1554370.tip: A cool autumn breeze ruffles Sue's sheep on the hill. Add a short u after the z, zu, and hold shii long like 'sheep': suzushii.

1556730.tip: A sumo wrestler puts on a tie straight from the freezer and shivers. Start with tsu, not su, and say me as 'meh', not 'mo': tsumetai.

1421970.tip: A snail inches toward the soy sauce by the sushi, so slow you sigh, 'Oh, soy...'. Pure o's, and soi rhymes with 'boy': osoi.

1214330.tip: Tan from a can is easy: one spray and you're done. Both a's are 'ah', not the a in 'can', and there's no d: kantan.

1474850.tip: Tom, a roo from the outback, stays the night at a hotel. Say to with a pure o, not 'tom', ma as 'mah', and a light, flicked ru: tomaru.

1005020.tip: ごろごろ is the sound of something heavy rolling. Picture yourself rolling from one end of the sofa to the other all day. Use a light, flicked r and keep every o short: gorogoro suru.

1553170-りょこうする-10.tip: 旅 ryo means 'journey', and 行 kō is the 行 of 行きます, 'go'. Add する, 'do', and you get 'to go on a journey'. Ryo is one beat, and the kō is long: ryokō suru.

1559160.tip: A wren practises sliding down a chute, over and over. Drop the t of 'chute' and hold the shū long. The n is a beat of its own: renshū suru.

1165970.tip: 一 ichi is 'one' and 番 ban is 'number', as in でんわばんごう. Number one is the best. Say ban as 'bahn', not 'ban': ichiban.

1189360.tip: Like どこ and どれ, ど asks a question. どっち is the casual way to pick between two. Pause on the small っ before chi: dotchi.

1189360-どちら-10.tip: This is the polite twin of どっち. It has the same ど question, no っ pause, and a ra on the end. Use it with teachers and shop staff: dochira.

1400150.tip: 早い hayai is 'early'. Swap its final い for く and it says how you do something: get up early. Say ha as 'hah', not 'hay': hayaku.

genki-10-あるいて.tip: A roo stops hopping and travels on foot, one step at a time. Keep ru short with a light flicked r, then say 'ee-teh': aruite.

1009010.tip: A doe stands at a yacht's wheel, wondering how to steer it. Hold the dō long, say ya as 'yah', and pause on the っ before te: dōyatte.

1009250.tip: どの dono is 'which', as in この and その, and ぐらい gurai is 'about'. 'About which amount' means how much or how long: donogurai.

genki-10-しゅうかん.tip: 週 shū is 'week', as in 来週 raishū, and 間 kan is a span of time, as in 時間 jikan. A span of weeks. Hold the shū long: -shūkan.

genki-10-かげつ.tip: 月 is 'month' and 'moon', read getsu as in getsuyōbi, and the small か counts them: 3か月 is three months. Say ka as 'kah': -kagetsu.

1004710.tip: この kono is 'this' and ごろ goro is 'around', as in 三時ごろ. 'Around this time' means these days. Keep every o short: konogoro.

genki-10-ご.tip: 後 go means 'after', as in 午後 gogo, 'after noon'. 一時間後 is an hour after now, so 'in an hour'. Use a short, pure o: -go.

1203620.tip: 外 gai is 'outside', and 国 koku is 'country', as in 中国 chūgoku and 韓国 kankoku. The country outside yours: gaikoku.

1390020.tip: A car drives straight into the river for a free car wash. Drop the 'sh' and keep both vowels a short 'ah': kawa.

1183450.tip: 温 is 'warm' and 泉 is 'spring': a warm spring, Japan's famous hot spring baths. Give each ん its own full beat, o-n-se-n: onsen.

1434040.tip: An eager angler goes fishing with two reels at once. Start with 'ts', keep the u short, make ri a light tap with no 'l', and drop the final s: tsuri.

1267280.tip: 水 mizu is 'water' and 海 umi is 'sea'. A sea of fresh water, sitting inland, is a lake. Say both u's, held a little: mizuumi.

1302680.tip: A llama climbs to the top of the mountain. Swap the 'l' for a 'y', and keep both vowels a short 'ah': yama.

1364670.tip: A knob of ginger is left as an offering at the shrine's gate. Keep jin short, and end on a clear 'jah', not 'jer': jinja.

1486460.tip: A bee sips from a juice can in front of a famous painting at the art museum. Short bi and ju, a light tsu, and kan like 'kahn': bijutsukan.

1322920.tip: 社 sha is from 会社 kaisha, 'company', and 長 chō means the head or chief. The company's chief is its president. Hold the ō long: shachō.

1193290.tip: A singer snacks on cashews between songs, a bowl balanced on the mic stand. Say ka as 'kah', not 'cash', and keep shu short: kashu.

1347710.tip: 来 rai means 'coming', as in 来年 rainen, next year. 将来 is the time still coming: the future. Hold the shō long: shōrai.

1604135.tip: Ma's tree is hung with lanterns for the town festival. Make tsu a 'ts' sound and ri a light tap, with the polite お in front: omatsuri.

2826498.tip: 月 gatsu is 'month', as in 一月 ichigatsu, and 正 shō means 'proper'. The proper first month is New Year's, with the polite お. Hold the shō long: oshōgatsu.

1001710.tip: The cashier slips you a free snack with your change. Say ka as a short 'kah', and end on a clean shi with no 'r', after the polite お: okashi.

1217070.tip: A wind-up toy carries a tiny mocha across the table. End on 'cha' as in 'chat', not 'kah', with a short o in front: omocha.

genki-11-こんがっき.tip: 今 kon is 'this', as in 今晩 konban, and 学期 gakki is a school term, 学 as in 学生 gakusei. Pause on the っ, gak-ki: kongakki.

1547810.tip: 来 rai is 'next', as in 来週 raishū, plus 学期 gakki, the school term. Pause on the っ before ki: raigakki.

1330290.tip: To start class, the teacher drops a yo-yo into a jug. Say ju as 'joo', not 'juh', and just one long yō: jugyō.

1004500.tip: こ is the 'near me' of これ, この and ここ. こちら is its polite form, for the person right beside you: 'This is Ms Tanaka.' Short, even beats: kochira.

1172440.tip: 'You sew a sock?' 'Yes!' says the boy, telling a lie: grandma sewed it. No y on the u, two o's in so-o, and tsu-ku, not 'sock': uso o tsuku.

2021520.tip: おなか is your stomach, が marks it, and すく means 'gets empty'. Staring at an empty plate, your stomach is empty, so you're hungry: onaka ga suku.

1312970.tip: 飼 has 食 'eat' on its left: the pet you keep is the one you feed every day. Same sound as 買う 'to buy', two short beats: kau.

1057580.tip: サボる comes from 'sabotage': you sabotage your own timetable by slipping out the door and cutting class. Sa-bo-ru, a short o and a flicked r: saboru.

1326980.tip: A tow truck hauls your textbooks to the lecture hall: you're taking the class. A short, pure o, not 'tow', then a light flicked ru, no 'truck': toru.

1333070.tip: A narwhal learns to write, gripping a pencil with its tusk. Three short beats, na-ra-u, a flicked r between the a's, ending on u, not 'whal': narau.

1352570.tip: 'No, boar!' shout the hikers as a wild boar climbs the mountain path after them. Three short beats: bo, not 'bore', then a flicked ru: noboru.

1402540.tip: Hashi is Japanese for chopsticks: picture a pair running across the table like two legs, then add ru. A light shi, three short beats: hashiru.

1483740.tip: A soccer roo plays ninety minutes, gets tired and flops on the grass. A hissed tsu, not 'so', ka like 'kah', re like 'reh', a short ru: tsukareru.

1318950.tip: Fed up with peeling, the cook drops the yam and quits on the spot. Ya-me-ru, three short beats, with me said like 'meh': yameru.

1257040.tip: Two boys have a fight over Ken's toy car. No z sound: the n is a beat of its own, then a crisp 'kah': kenka suru.

1351430.tip: You lift your new friend up beside the trophy showcase to introduce her to everyone. Hold the shō long, and kai rhymes with 'sky', not 'case': shōkai suru.

1422050.tip: The cheeky cuckoo is late again, popping out of its clock long after the hour. Drop the 'ky': just chi, then a short ko-ku: chikoku suru.

1552740.tip: 留 ryū is 'stay', and 学 gaku is 'study', as in daigaku and gakusei. You fly off to stay somewhere and study: ryūgaku suru.

1339260.tip: 出 is the 'come out' of 出る, and 身 is 'body': the place your body came out from, your hometown. Hold the っ as a short pause before shin: shusshin.

1227370.tip: An old friend turns up holding his ashy brie under a spider web: it's been ages. Say hi-sa, not 'hiz', and bu-ri as two beats, not 'bree': hisashiburi.

1012070.tip: Mama tastes your first curry and tilts her hand: okay, not bad. Hold both a's long and flat, maa-maa, not a quick 'mama': māmā.

1012620.tip: The gym's motto, painted on an old scroll, is one word: more. Pause on the っ before to, and keep both o's short and pure, not 'mah-toe': motto.

1269320.tip: After the race, a runner soaks a sore toe. Say a clear 'ah', not 'uh', and a short pure to, not 'toe': ato.

1297510.tip: A writer signs her novel's last line on a soccer ball. Say sa, not 'so', pause at the っ, and end on a clear 'kah', not 'ker': sakka.

1471970.tip: An actor plays Romeo from a high yew tree, calling down to Juliet. Hai is one quick beat, and hold the yū long: haiyū.

1252400.tip: A police officer stops Kay and inspects her satsuma can. No z after kei, drop the 'ma', and kan rhymes with 'khan', not 'can': keisatsukan.

1350350.tip: Firefighters spray water on a burning showboat. Drop the t, add a quick shi, and hold both o's long and pure: shōbōshi.

1811920.tip: 漫画 manga, plus 家 ka, a professional, as in sakka the writer. The one who draws manga: mangaka.

1237130.tip: 教 kyō is 'teach', as in kyōkasho, the textbook, and 師 shi is a master of a craft. Hold the kyō long: kyōshi.

1258590.tip: 研究 kenkyū is 'research', and 者 sha is 'person', as in isha, the doctor. Hold the kyū long, in one beat: kenkyūsha.

1171400.tip: 宇宙 uchū is 'space', 飛行 hikō is 'flight', as in hikōki, and 士 shi is a professional, as in bengoshi. A space-flight professional: uchū hikōshi.

2403340.tip: スポーツ is just 'sports'. 選 sen is 'chosen', and 手 is 'hand', the te of tegami, read shu here: a chosen hand, a player. Together: supōtsu senshu.

1414650.tip: 大 dai is 'big', as in daigaku, and 統領 tōryō is 'chief': the big chief. Hold both o's long, and ryo is one syllable, not 'ree-oh': daitōryō.

1002610.tip: He lies belly-up on a car, patting his full stomach in the sun. A pure o, not 'on', and a short, open ka with no r: onaka.

1404630.tip: Campfire ash falls and coats his bare leg grey. Say a as in 'ah', not the a of 'ash', then add a short i: ashi.

1600280.tip: A dry lump of dough sticks in his throat, and he croaks 'No dough!' Two short, pure o's, not the gliding 'doh' of dough: nodo.

1313000.tip: 'Ha!' A big laugh shows off every tooth. Keep it short and open, like 'hah': ha.

1583720.tip: 風 kaze is 'wind', as in kamikaze, 'divine wind', and 邪 means 'evil'. An evil wind blows in a cold: kaze.

1602760.tip: 二日 futsuka is 'two days', as in the 2nd of the month, and 酔い yoi is 'drunkenness'. Still drunk on day two: futsukayoi.

1549140.tip: The egg-shaped Tamagotchi pet takes its name from tamago, 'egg'. Drop the -tchi and say three short beats, ta-ma-go: tamago.

1502390.tip: Through his monocle, the collector squints at a strange little thing. Two short, pure o's, 'moh-noh': mono.

1385170.tip: The conductor punches a hole in a kipper instead of your train ticket. Pause on the っ between kip and pu, and end on a short u, not 'er': kippu.

1546300.tip: The yogi rolls up his mat: he has business to take care of in town. Hold the yō long, and say ji as in 'jeep', not yogi's hard g: yōji.

1002100.tip: お is polite, 手 te is 'hand' and 洗い arai is 'washing', from 洗う arau. The polite hand-washing place: otearai.

1312420.tip: 試 shi is 'try', as in 試験 shiken, 'exam', and 合 ai is 'together'. Trying your strength against each other is a match, in three beats, shi-a-i: shiai.

1483150.tip: She cracks open a can o' joe, her morning coffee. Say ka as 'kah', not 'can', then two short o's, no-jo: kanojo.

1483070.tip: 彼 means 'that person over there'. Alone it is kare, 'he'; add 女 'woman' and it is kanojo, 'she'. Short a, tapped r, short e, not 'curry': kare.

1483140.tip: 彼 kare 'he' plus 氏 shi, a polite word for a man. Your own special 'he' is your boyfriend: kareshi.

1237680.tip: A semi truck squeezes down a narrow alley, its mirrors scraping the walls. Say it 'sem-eye', with a short e and an open ma: semai.

1278410.tip: A heron spreads its wings wide across the whole lake. Say hi as 'hee', not 'heh', tap a short ro with no n, then add a short i: hiroi.

1432680.tip: A tie knotted far too tight hurts your neck. Start with a short ee, not 'uh', and say tai just like 'tie': itai.

1213400.tip: A mime pretends to lick a giant lollipop: so sweet! Say ah, not 'uh', and drop the final m: amai.

1397350.tip: A sizzling steak arrives at the table: how nice! The su is barely voiced, te is short as in 'ten', not 'stay', and end on ki: suteki.

1514320.tip: Our cook walks to the market every morning. Say ah, tap the r like a quick d, and end on a short ku, not 'cook': aruku.

1499880.tip: 風邪 kaze is written 'wind' plus 'evil': a bad wind blows in and you catch (hiku) a cold. Short a, and zeh, not 'zee': kaze o hiku.

genki-12-ねつがある.tip: A goalie with a fever lies limp in the nets. Netsu is 'nets' with a faint u, and ga aru is 'there is': netsu ga aru.

1277350.tip: のど nodo is 'throat'. Kawaku, 'to dry out', starts like kawa, 'river': picture a river gone dry, and your throat with it: nodo ga kawaku.

1606590.tip: Don't mix it up with wakaru, 'understand': this one adds re. Couples who stop understanding each other break up: wakareru.

1241880.tip: A king trembles before his big show on stage. Say kin, not 'king', use ch, not sh, and hold the chō long: kinchō suru.

1360930.tip: A chimp frets over his pie, checking it again and again. Start with sh, not ch, and the ん sounds like m before p: shinpai suru.

1002390.tip: Polite お plus 大事 daiji, 'precious', with the same 大 dai as daijōbu: 'treat yourself as precious', said to someone who's ill: odaiji ni.

genki-12-げんきがない.tip: You know genki from o-genki desu ka, and ga nai means 'there isn't any'. No genki left at all: genki ga nai.

1340460.tip: できる dekiru is 'can do' and だけ dake is 'just': just as much as you can do. Keep every syllable short: dekiru dake.

2015610.tip: もう mō is 'already' and すぐ sugu is 'right away': it's practically already here. Hold the mō long: mōsugu.

1342550.tip: Shorten hajimemashite, 'nice to meet you', which you say when meeting someone for the first time. Drop the mashi: hajimete.

1007040.tip: それ sore is 'that' and に ni adds 'to': to that, add one more thing. Say it as one smooth word: soreni.
